 Follow 15 Players Share New York Lottery Jackpot After Winning with Consecutive Numbers
 Geca Flores Wed, November 18, 2026 at 5:33 AM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. 15 Players Share New York Lottery Jackpot After Winning with Consecutive Numbers The New York Lottery sparked buzz after an extraordinary stroke of luck resulted in multiple players sharing the jackpot following an unusually rare combination in the Take 5 Evening draw.
 On Nov. 14, lottery players tuned in for that evening's drawing, hoping to match all five winning numbers and claim the coveted jackpot.
 However, many were stunned when the results revealed a unique selection of numbers.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The winning numbers were 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14, a sequence of five consecutive numbers that led to an unexpected outcome.
 Unfortunately, Saturday's drawing produced 15 winning tickets, meaning the $32,587.50 combined prize pool would be divided equally among the winners.
 As a result, each lucky ticket holder would receive a much smaller share of the total prize, approximately $2,172.50, rather than the full jackpot.
 Unlike major multi-state jackpot games such as Powerball and Mega Millions, Take 5 Evening features a much smaller number pool, ranging from 1 to 39.
 This increases the likelihood of multiple players selecting the same winning combination, making it more common for jackpots to be shared among several winners.
 Advertisement Advertisement Meanwhile, the New York Lottery reminded players that they still have opportunities to win big through scratch-off games.
 Several of these games have unclaimed top prizes, including jackpots that could make lucky players instant millionaires, according to WIBX950. 
 While this drawing offers a fascinating story of luck, it is not the first time a lottery jackpot has been shared among multiple winners.
 On Jan. 26, 1991, nine ticket holders with matching winning numbers split the $90 million Super Lotto jackpot. 
 The winning tickets were sold in Manhattan, Brooklyn, the Bronx, Queens, Yonkers, Rockland County and Suffolk County, according to the New York Lottery's historical records.
 Advertisement Advertisement Winners from Brooklyn, the Bronx, Manhattan, Queens, Rockland County, Suffolk County and Yonkers each received $10 million, paid out over 20 years. According to New York Lotto spokeswoman Ann Doyle, the jackpot was the nation's third-largest at the time.
 In December 2024, another unusual sequence appeared in the Mega Millions drawing , with four consecutive numbers: 66, 67, 68 and 69.
